'This' refers to something close in space or time. It helps identify a specific object or idea. This draws attention to something immediate. It can describe physical items or abstract concepts. The word clarifies focus in conversation. This helps distinguish from other possibilities. It makes communication precise.

'What' is a word used to ask for information. It helps identify things, actions, or reasons. What shows curiosity or confusion. It is used in both simple and complex questions. The word guides communication and clarity. It directs others to explain or specify something. What is essential for understanding details.

'Evening' is the time at the end of the day, usually after the afternoon and before night. Evening shows a period of the day. People notice the late hours. It is a noun. It shows time. For example, 'We had dinner in the evening' means the meal happened during that late part of the day.

'External' means something that is on the outside or comes from outside. External shows outer position or origin. People notice outside source. It is an adjective. It shows location or origin. For example, 'external damage' means damage on the outside surface, and 'external pressure' means pressure coming from outside.

'Expand' means to become larger or to make something bigger. Expand shows growth or increase. People notice size change. It is a verb. It shows enlargement. For example, 'The company wants to expand its business' means they want to grow bigger. It can also mean to explain in more detail.

'Effort' means the energy or work you put into doing something. Effort shows hard work or trying. People notice dedication. It is a noun. It shows exertion. For example, 'She put a lot of effort into her project' means she worked very hard on it.

'Pure' means something is clean, without any mixture or bad things added. Pure shows cleanliness or completeness. People notice quality or innocence. It is an adjective. It shows unmixed state. For example, 'pure water' means water with nothing else in it, and 'pure joy' means happiness with no other feelings mixed in.

'Federal' relates to a system of government where several states are united under one central authority. Federal shows government structure. People notice central authority. It is an adjective. It shows national or central power. For example, 'federal law' means a law that applies across all states in a country.

'Gross' can mean the total amount before any deductions, or it can describe something very unpleasant. Gross shows total amount or disgust. People notice full amount or bad feeling. It is an adjective or noun. For example, 'gross income' means all money earned before taxes, and 'That is so gross' means something is very disgusting.

'Cover' means to place something over another thing to protect or hide it, or to include a topic. Cover shows protection or inclusion. People notice something placed over. It is a verb or noun. It shows wrapping or range. For example, 'Cover the pot with a lid' means put something on top, and 'The book covers many topics' means it includes them.

'Boyfriend' refers to a male person someone is in a romantic relationship with. Boyfriend shows romantic connection. People notice personal relationship. It is a noun. It shows partnership. For example, 'She introduced her boyfriend to her family' means she introduced the man she is dating to them.

'Nature' refers to the natural world including plants, animals, and landscapes, or the basic qualities of something. Nature shows the natural world or essential character. People notice environment or quality. It is a noun. For example, 'We went for a walk in nature' means in the natural environment, and 'It is his nature to be kind' means kindness is his basic character.

'Anyway' is used to return to a topic or to show that something is true regardless of other things. Anyway shows continuation or dismissal. People notice a shift in conversation. It is an adverb. It shows refocus. For example, 'Anyway, let us get back to the main point' means moving back to the subject.

'Note' means a short written message or to pay careful attention to something. Note shows record or attention. People notice written reminder. It is a noun or verb. It shows observation or writing. For example, 'She left a note on the table' means a short written message, and 'Please note the time' means pay attention to it.

'Game' refers to an activity done for fun or competition, usually with rules. Game shows play or competition. People notice fun or challenge. It is a noun. It shows entertainment. For example, 'Let us play a game' means to do a fun activity together, and 'The game starts at seven' means a sporting event.

'Improve' means to make something better or to become better. Improve shows positive change. People notice getting better. It is a verb. It shows progress. For example, 'I want to improve my English' means to become better at English. It shows a move from a lower level to a higher one.

'Impact' means a strong effect on something or someone. Impact shows influence or result. People notice a big change. It is a noun or verb. It shows effect. For example, 'The rain had a big impact on the game' means the rain greatly affected the game. It can also mean a physical collision.

'Shut' means to close something or to stop something from being open. Shut shows closing action. People notice something closed. It is a verb or adjective. It shows closed state. For example, 'Please shut the door' means close the door, and 'The shop is shut' means it is not open.

'Entry' means the act of going into a place, or a piece of information recorded somewhere. Entry shows access or record. People notice entering or registering. It is a noun. It shows going in or noting down. For example, 'No entry' means you cannot go in, and 'Please fill in your entry' means write your information.

'Officer' refers to a person with authority, especially in the police, military, or government. Officer shows rank or authority. People notice position of power. It is a noun. It shows official role. For example, 'The police officer stopped the car' means a person with police authority stopped it.

'Finally' means after a long time or at the end of a series of events. Finally shows conclusion or last step. People notice something long awaited. It is an adverb. It shows the end. For example, 'She finally arrived' means she arrived after a long wait. It shows relief or completion.

'Selection' means the process of choosing something, or a group of things available to choose from. Selection shows choice or variety. People notice options or choosing. It is a noun. It shows picking. For example, 'There is a wide selection of food' means many choices are available.

'Steps' refers to the individual actions in a process, or the physical act of walking movement. Steps shows progression or movement. People notice stages or footsteps. It is a noun. It shows sequence or walking. For example, 'Follow these steps to set it up' means do each action in order, and 'She took small steps' means she walked carefully.

'Computer' is an electronic machine that processes and stores information. Computer shows technology or device. People notice digital tool. It is a noun. It shows electronic machine. For example, 'I use a computer for work' means using an electronic device to do tasks.

'Joint' refers to a place where two things are connected, or something shared between two or more people. Joint shows connection or sharing. People notice shared or linked things. It is a noun or adjective. It shows combined effort. For example, 'a joint project' means a project done together, and 'the knee joint' means where bones meet.

'Lose' means to no longer have something, or to fail to win. Lose shows loss or defeat. People notice something missing or a game lost. It is a verb. It shows failure or disappearance. For example, 'I always lose my keys' means I cannot find them, and 'We might lose the match' means not win.

'Copy' means to make something exactly the same as the original, or a duplicate of something. Copy shows reproduction or duplication. People notice a repeated item. It is a noun or verb. It shows replication. For example, 'Please make a copy of this document' means produce an identical version of it.

'Strike' means to hit something hard, or when workers stop working to protest. Strike shows hitting or protesting. People notice impact or worker action. It is a verb or noun. It shows force or refusal. For example, 'The workers went on strike' means they stopped working to demand better conditions.

'Initial' means something that happens at the very beginning, or the first letter of a name. Initial shows starting point. People notice early stage. It is an adjective or noun. It shows beginning. For example, 'my initial reaction' means what I felt at first, and 'Sign your initials' means write the first letters of your name.

'Sword' is a long sharp weapon with a blade used for fighting. Sword shows weapon or combat tool. People notice blade or fighting. It is a noun. It shows weapon. For example, 'The knight carried a sword' means he had a long bladed weapon with him.

'Progress' means moving forward or improving over time. Progress shows improvement or advancement. People notice development. It is a noun or verb. It shows forward movement. For example, 'She is making great progress in her studies' means she is getting better and learning more.

'Winter' is the coldest season of the year. Winter shows cold season. People notice cold weather and short days. It is a noun. It shows seasonal time. For example, 'It snows a lot in winter' means during the coldest season of the year.

'Afraid' means feeling fear or worry about something. Afraid shows fear or anxiety. People notice frightened feeling. It is an adjective. It shows scared state. For example, 'She is afraid of spiders' means spiders make her feel fear. It can also mean being worried about a situation.

'Directly' means in a straight line, without going anywhere else first, or in a clear and honest way. Directly shows straight path or frankness. People notice clear or immediate action. It is an adverb. It shows no detour. For example, 'Go directly home' means go home without stopping anywhere.

'Intense' describes something very strong, serious, or extreme. Intense shows high level or strength. People notice powerful feeling or situation. It is an adjective. It shows great degree. For example, 'intense heat' means very strong heat, and 'an intense game' means a very serious and exciting competition.

'Buffer' refers to something that helps reduce the impact between two things, or a temporary storage area in computing. Buffer shows protection or temporary storage. People notice spacing or delay. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'a buffer zone' means a neutral area between two sides, and 'the video is buffering' means it is loading data.

'Sharp' describes something with a very thin edge that can cut easily, or a sudden and strong sensation. Sharp shows cutting ability or strong feeling. People notice thin edge or sudden change. It is an adjective. For example, 'a sharp knife' means one that cuts easily, and 'a sharp pain' means a sudden strong pain.

'Student' refers to a person who is learning at a school or university. Student shows learner or academic member. People notice someone studying. It is a noun. It shows educational role. For example, 'She is a student at the university' means she attends and studies there.

'Capacity' means the maximum amount something can hold, or the ability to do something. Capacity shows limit or ability. People notice maximum space or potential. It is a noun. It shows capability. For example, 'The hall has a capacity of 500 people' means it can hold that many, and 'She has the capacity to lead' means she has the ability.

'Series' refers to a number of things that come one after another in a connected order. Series shows sequence or set. People notice connected items. It is a noun. It shows ordered group. For example, 'a series of events' means events happening one after another, and 'a TV series' means a show with multiple connected episodes.

'Horse' is a large four-legged animal used for riding or carrying loads. Horse shows large animal. People notice farm or riding animal. It is a noun. It shows animal. For example, 'She rode the horse across the field' means she sat on the animal and it carried her.

'Unable' means not having the ability or power to do something. Unable shows lack of ability. People notice limitation. It is an adjective. It shows incapability. For example, 'I am unable to attend the meeting' means I cannot be there. It is the opposite of able.

'Elegant' describes something that is graceful, stylish, and attractive in a simple way. Elegant shows grace or refined style. People notice beauty and simplicity. It is an adjective. It shows sophistication. For example, 'She wore an elegant dress' means a graceful and stylish dress.

'Daily' means happening or done every day. Daily shows regular occurrence. People notice everyday pattern. It is an adjective or adverb. It shows frequency. For example, 'daily exercise' means exercise done every day, and 'I check my email daily' means every single day.

'Check' means to look at something carefully to see if it is correct or in good condition. Check shows inspection or verification. People notice looking for errors. It is a verb or noun. It shows examination. For example, 'Check your answers before submitting' means look over them carefully.

'Weekend' refers to Saturday and Sunday, the days when most people do not work. Weekend shows rest period. People notice free time. It is a noun. It shows two days off. For example, 'I will visit you this weekend' means on Saturday or Sunday.

'Tonne' is a unit of weight equal to one thousand kilograms. Tonne shows measurement or weight. People notice large quantity. It is a noun. It shows metric unit. For example, 'The truck carries five tonnes of goods' means five thousand kilograms of items.

'Million' is the number one thousand thousands, written as 1,000,000. Million shows a very large quantity. People notice big number. It is a noun or adjective. It shows large amount. For example, 'one million people' means 1,000,000 individuals, and 'a million dollars' means a very large sum of money.

'Block' means a solid piece of material, or to stop something from passing through. Block shows obstacle or solid shape. People notice prevention or solid object. It is a noun or verb. It shows stopping or solid form. For example, 'a block of wood' is a solid piece, and 'block the road' means stop people from using it.

'Watching' means looking at something carefully over a period of time. Watching shows observation or attention. People notice visual focus. It is a verb. It shows continuous looking. For example, 'She is watching the game' means she is giving her attention to the game as it happens.

'Quota' means a fixed number or share of something that is expected or allowed. Quota shows limit or target. People notice assigned amount. It is a noun. It shows required portion. For example, 'a sales quota' means the number of sales a person must reach, and 'import quota' means the limit on goods allowed in.

'Truth' means the real facts about something, the opposite of a lie. Truth shows reality or honesty. People notice what is real. It is a noun. It shows accurate information. For example, 'Please tell me the truth' means share what actually happened, not what is false.

'Military' relates to the armed forces of a country, such as the army, navy, and air force. Military shows armed forces or defense. People notice soldiers or weapons. It is an adjective or noun. It shows organized armed power. For example, 'military training' means training done by or for soldiers.

'Dinner' is the main meal of the day, usually eaten in the evening. Dinner shows mealtime. People notice food and gathering. It is a noun. It shows evening meal. For example, 'We had dinner at seven' means the main meal was eaten at that time.

'Parts' refers to pieces or sections that make up a whole. Parts shows components or sections. People notice individual pieces. It is a noun. It shows division of a whole. For example, 'The machine has many parts' means it is made up of many separate pieces that work together.

'Follow' means to go after someone or something, or to act according to instructions. Follow shows coming after or obeying. People notice movement behind or compliance. It is a verb. It shows tracking or compliance. For example, 'Follow me' means come after me, and 'Follow the rules' means obey them.

'Pick' means to choose something from a group, or to take something from a place. Pick shows selection or taking. People notice choosing. It is a verb or noun. It shows choice. For example, 'Pick the one you like best' means choose your favorite, and 'She picked a flower' means she took a flower from where it was.

'Song' is a short piece of music with words that are sung. Song shows music and vocals. People notice melody and lyrics. It is a noun. It shows musical piece. For example, 'She sang a beautiful song' means she performed a piece of music using her voice.

'Language' is a system of words and rules used to communicate with others. Language shows communication system. People notice words and grammar. It is a noun. It shows means of expression. For example, 'English is a language spoken by many people around the world' means it is one system of communication used widely.

'Carry' means to hold and move something from one place to another. Carry shows transport or holding. People notice bringing or supporting weight. It is a verb. It shows moving with. For example, 'Can you carry this bag for me?' means hold and bring the bag.

'Spot' means a particular place or location, or a small mark on a surface. Spot shows location or mark. People notice a specific place or a stain. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'This is a great spot for a picnic' means a nice location, and 'I spotted her in the crowd' means I noticed her.

'Wall' is a vertical solid structure that divides or surrounds an area. Wall shows barrier or structure. People notice solid division or boundary. It is a noun. It shows dividing surface. For example, 'There is a wall between the two rooms' means a solid structure separates them.

'Wood' is the hard material that comes from trees, used for building or fuel. Wood shows natural material. People notice trees or building material. It is a noun. It shows tree material. For example, 'The table is made of wood' means the material used is from a tree.

'Simply' means in a plain or easy way, or used to emphasize something. Simply shows ease or emphasis. People notice plainness or stress. It is an adverb. It shows clarity. For example, 'Just do it simply' means without complication, and 'It is simply the best' means nothing more than the best.

'Mature' means fully grown or developed, or behaving in a sensible adult way. Mature shows full development or responsible behavior. People notice grown-up attitude. It is an adjective or verb. It shows development. For example, 'She is very mature for her age' means she acts responsibly like an adult.

'Onto' means moving to a position on top of or into contact with something. Onto shows direction and surface contact. People notice movement to a surface. It is a preposition. It shows movement to a place. For example, 'She climbed onto the roof' means she moved upward and got on top of it.

'Mineral' is a natural solid substance found in the earth, such as iron or gold. Mineral shows natural material. People notice earth resource or nutrition. It is a noun. It shows natural element. For example, 'The body needs minerals like calcium and iron to stay healthy' means natural substances are needed.

'Mail' refers to letters and packages sent through the postal system, or to send something by post. Mail shows delivery system. People notice letters or packages. It is a noun or verb. It shows postal communication. For example, 'I received mail today' means letters or packages arrived for me.

'Manner' means the way in which something is done or happens, or a person's behavior toward others. Manner shows style or behavior. People notice how something is done. It is a noun. It shows approach or conduct. For example, 'She spoke in a polite manner' means she spoke in a respectful way.

'Discontinued' means something has been stopped or is no longer available. Discontinued shows ending or stopping. People notice something no longer continuing. It is an adjective. It shows cessation. For example, 'This product has been discontinued' means the company no longer makes or sells it.

'Auto' is a short word for automobile, meaning a car. Auto shows vehicle or self-operating. People notice a car or automatic function. It is a noun or prefix. It shows car or automatic. For example, 'He bought a new auto' means a new car, and 'auto-correct' means it corrects automatically.

'Strange' means unusual, unfamiliar, or difficult to understand. Strange shows oddness or unfamiliarity. People notice something different from normal. It is an adjective. It shows unusual quality. For example, 'That is a strange noise' means an unusual sound that is hard to explain.

'Lay' means to put something down gently in a flat position. Lay shows placing action. People notice putting something flat. It is a verb. It shows horizontal placement. For example, 'Lay the book on the table' means place it flat. It is different from 'lie' which refers to a person resting.

'Leaving' means going away from a place or person. Leaving shows departing action. People notice someone going away. It is a verb. It shows departure. For example, 'She is leaving for work now' means she is going away to her workplace.

'Declared' means something was officially announced or stated clearly. Declared shows formal announcement. People notice official statement. It is a verb. It shows proclamation. For example, 'The president declared a national holiday' means he officially announced it to everyone.

'Piece' refers to a part or section of something larger. Piece shows a portion or part. People notice a separated section. It is a noun. It shows individual part. For example, 'a piece of cake' means one portion of a larger cake, and 'a piece of music' means one musical work.

'Operation' refers to an organized activity or process, or a medical procedure. Operation shows organized action or medical work. People notice process or surgery. It is a noun. It shows planned activity. For example, 'a military operation' means an organized mission, and 'heart operation' means surgery on the heart.

'Remaining' means still present or left over after others have gone. Remaining shows what is left. People notice leftover items. It is an adjective or verb. It shows the rest of something. For example, 'the remaining students' means those who are still there after others have left.

'Event' refers to a thing that happens, especially something important or planned. Event shows happening or occasion. People notice scheduled activity. It is a noun. It shows occurrence. For example, 'The sports event was attended by thousands' means many people came to watch the planned activity.

'Prepared' means ready for something or having made something in advance. Prepared shows readiness. People notice being ready. It is an adjective or verb. It shows prior action. For example, 'I am prepared for the exam' means I have studied and am ready, and 'She prepared dinner' means she made it beforehand.

'Eating' means the act of putting food in your mouth and swallowing it. Eating shows consuming food. People notice the action of having a meal. It is a verb. It shows food consumption. For example, 'He is eating his lunch' means he is having his midday meal right now.

'Cent' is a small unit of money equal to one hundredth of a dollar or euro. Cent shows small currency. People notice small monetary value. It is a noun. It shows money unit. For example, 'This candy costs fifty cents' means it is half of one dollar.

'Doctor' is a person trained in medicine who treats sick or injured people. Doctor shows medical professional. People notice health care worker. It is a noun. It shows trained healer. For example, 'I went to see the doctor about my cough' means I visited a medical professional for treatment.

'Code' refers to a set of rules or symbols used to represent information, or instructions written for computers. Code shows system of symbols or instructions. People notice hidden language or programming. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'Type the code to unlock it' means enter the secret symbols, and 'She wrote code for the app' means she programmed it.

'Volume' refers to the amount of space something takes up, the level of sound, or a book in a series. Volume shows quantity or sound level. People notice space, loudness, or a book. It is a noun. For example, 'Turn up the volume' means make it louder, and 'a large volume of water' means a large amount.

'Flash' means a sudden bright light, or to appear very quickly. Flash shows quick brightness or speed. People notice sudden light or fast movement. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'a flash of lightning' means a sudden burst of light, and 'The answer flashed in my mind' means it came suddenly.

'Monetary' relates to money or the system of money in a country. Monetary shows financial system. People notice money-related matters. It is an adjective. It shows connection to currency. For example, 'monetary policy' means decisions a government makes about money supply and interest rates.

'Exactly' means precisely, without any difference. Exactly shows precision or agreement. People notice accurate match. It is an adverb. It shows completeness. For example, 'That is exactly what I meant' means it matches perfectly what was intended.

'Throw' means to send something through the air by moving your hand quickly. Throw shows tossing action. People notice something sent through the air. It is a verb or noun. It shows physical act. For example, 'Throw the ball to me' means send it through the air in my direction.

'Nation' refers to a country and all the people who live in it. Nation shows country or people. People notice shared land and culture. It is a noun. It shows political and social group. For example, 'The whole nation celebrated the victory' means everyone in the country shared in the happiness.

'Division' means the act of separating something into parts, or a section of a larger organization. Division shows separation or section. People notice splitting or organizing. It is a noun. It shows splitting apart. For example, 'the sales division' means a section of a company, and 'division of tasks' means splitting up the work.

'Purpose' means the reason something exists or the goal of an action. Purpose shows intention or goal. People notice reason behind action. It is a noun. It shows aim. For example, 'The purpose of this meeting is to solve the problem' means the reason for holding it.

'Warm' means having a comfortable level of heat, or showing kindness and friendliness. Warm shows pleasant heat or friendly feeling. People notice gentle heat or kind attitude. It is an adjective or verb. For example, 'warm weather' means comfortably hot, and 'a warm welcome' means a friendly greeting.

'Interested' means having attention or curiosity toward something. Interested shows curiosity or attention. People notice engagement or enthusiasm. It is an adjective. It shows attraction to a topic. For example, 'She is interested in science' means she finds science engaging and wants to know more about it.

'Names' refers to the words used to identify people, places, or things. Names shows identity labels. People notice identification words. It is a noun. It shows labels given to things. For example, 'She wrote all the names on the list' means she recorded the identifying words for each person.

'Produce' means to make or create something, or fresh food such as vegetables and fruit. Produce shows creation or fresh food. People notice making or growing. It is a verb or noun. For example, 'The factory produces cars' means it makes them, and 'fresh produce' means fresh vegetables and fruit from a farm.

'Effects' refers to the results or changes caused by something. Effects shows results or consequences. People notice changes produced. It is a noun. It shows outcomes. For example, 'the effects of the storm' means the damage and changes the storm caused.

'Loaded' means filled with something, especially a heavy amount, or ready to fire. Loaded shows being full or ready. People notice a full or ready state. It is an adjective. It shows filled condition. For example, 'a loaded truck' means a truck filled with goods, and 'a loaded gun' means one ready to fire.

'Broke' is the past tense of break, meaning something was broken. It also informally means having no money. Broke shows broken state or lack of money. People notice damage or poverty. It is a verb or adjective. For example, 'She broke the glass' means it shattered, and 'I am broke' means I have no money.

'Sat' is the past tense of sit, meaning someone was in a seated position. Sat shows past sitting action. People notice previous seating. It is a verb. It shows past resting in a seat. For example, 'He sat on the chair for an hour' means he was seated there for that time.

'Commercial' relates to trade and business, or an advertisement on TV or radio. Commercial shows business activity or advertisement. People notice trade or ads. It is an adjective or noun. For example, 'a commercial building' means one used for business, and 'a TV commercial' means a short advertisement.

'Corner' refers to the point where two lines, walls, or streets meet. Corner shows meeting point or angle. People notice edge or junction. It is a noun. It shows where two things meet. For example, 'Meet me at the corner of the street' means at the point where two streets meet.

'Fairly' means to a moderate degree, or in a way that is just and honest. Fairly shows moderate level or justice. People notice reasonable amount or fair treatment. It is an adverb. For example, 'It is fairly easy' means not very hard but not too simple, and 'She was treated fairly' means justly.

'Police' refers to the official organization responsible for maintaining law and order. Police shows law enforcement. People notice officers or authority. It is a noun or verb. It shows order-keeping institution. For example, 'Call the police' means contact the law enforcement authorities for help.

'Pound' is a unit of weight, or the currency used in the UK. It can also mean to hit something repeatedly with force. Pound shows weight, currency, or hitting. People notice measurement, money, or strong blows. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'It costs five pounds' means five units of British currency.

'Generally' means in most cases or usually. Generally shows common occurrence. People notice broad pattern. It is an adverb. It shows overall tendency. For example, 'People generally prefer warm weather' means most people tend to prefer it.

'Marketing' is the activity of promoting and selling products or services. Marketing shows promotion and business strategy. People notice advertising and sales. It is a noun. It shows commercial communication. For example, 'The marketing team created a new campaign to attract more customers' means they made a plan to promote the product.

'Sight' refers to the ability to see, or something that is seen. Sight shows vision or visible scene. People notice seeing ability or a view. It is a noun. It shows visual experience. For example, 'The sight of the mountains was beautiful' means the view of them was stunning.

'Concern' means to worry about something, or a matter that is important to someone. Concern shows worry or importance. People notice care or anxiety. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'I have a concern about the plan' means I am worried about something in it.

'Primary' means first in order, most important, or basic. Primary shows highest priority or first level. People notice main or first thing. It is an adjective. It shows first importance. For example, 'primary school' means the first level of formal education.

'Built' is the past tense of build, meaning something was constructed. Built shows completed construction. People notice something made or created. It is a verb. It shows past construction. For example, 'The bridge was built in 1990' means construction finished in that year.

'Material' refers to the substance or matter from which something is made, or something relevant to a situation. Material shows physical substance or relevance. People notice fabric or important information. It is a noun or adjective. For example, 'The dress is made of soft material' means the fabric is soft.

'Weird' means very strange or unusual in a way that is hard to explain. Weird shows oddness or unexpectedness. People notice something out of the ordinary. It is an adjective. It shows strangeness. For example, 'That is a weird thing to say' means it is an unusual or unexpected statement.

'Senior' refers to someone who is older or higher in rank or position. Senior shows higher rank or older age. People notice experience or authority. It is an adjective or noun. For example, 'a senior manager' means one with higher rank, and 'senior citizens' means older members of society.

'Respectively' means in the order mentioned, each one matching the other. Respectively shows matching order. People notice paired sequence. It is an adverb. It shows corresponding order. For example, 'Tom and Jane won first and second place respectively' means Tom won first and Jane won second.

'Weather' refers to the conditions outside such as rain, sunshine, wind, or temperature. Weather shows atmospheric conditions. People notice outdoor climate. It is a noun. It shows daily climate state. For example, 'The weather today is cold and rainy' means the outside conditions include low temperature and rain.

'Attack' means to use violence against someone or something, or to criticize strongly. Attack shows aggression or criticism. People notice harmful action. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'The army launched an attack' means they started a violent operation, and 'She attacked his idea' means she criticized it strongly.

'Pause' means to stop temporarily before continuing. Pause shows brief stop. People notice a moment of waiting. It is a noun or verb. It shows temporary halt. For example, 'Pause the video' means stop it briefly, and 'There was a pause in the conversation' means a moment of silence.

'Pull' means to move something toward yourself by gripping and drawing it. Pull shows drawing motion. People notice something moved toward them. It is a verb or noun. It shows pulling force. For example, 'Pull the door to open it' means drag it toward you, and 'the pull of gravity' means the force that attracts things.

'Throughout' means in every part of something, or all the way through a period of time. Throughout shows complete coverage. People notice something happening everywhere or the whole time. 'Sterling' refers to British money, or something of excellent quality. Sterling shows British currency or high quality. People notice monetary value or excellent standard. It is an adjective or noun. For example, 'The price is fifty pounds sterling' means fifty units of British currency.

'Column' refers to a tall vertical structure used for support, or a vertical section in a table or article. Column shows vertical structure or arrangement. 'Somebody' means an unspecified person. Somebody shows reference to an unnamed person. People notice that a person exists. It is a pronoun. For example, 'Somebody left their bag here' means an unspecified person forgot it.

'Operate' means to use or control a machine, or to perform surgery. Operate shows controlling machinery or performing medical procedure. People notice working a device or medical action. It is a verb. For example, 'She learned to operate the machine' means she learned how to use and control it.

'Loud' means making a lot of noise, or having strong bright colors. Loud shows high volume of sound. People notice strong noise or striking appearance. It is an adjective or adverb. For example, 'The music was very loud' means it made a strong, powerful sound.

'Dialogue' refers to a conversation between two or more people, or written conversation in a book or film. Dialogue shows verbal or written exchange. People notice two-way communication. 'Supported' means given help, encouragement, or held up physically. Supported shows help received or physical backing. People notice something held up or helped. It is a verb or adjective. For example, 'Her friends supported her decision' means they agreed with and encouraged it.

'Fallen' is the past participle of fall, meaning something has dropped or gone down. Fallen shows completed downward movement. People notice something that has dropped. It is a verb or adjective. For example, 'The tree has fallen across the road' means it has dropped and now blocks the path.

'Hide' means to put something in a place where others cannot find it, or to stay out of sight. Hide shows concealing. People notice keeping something secret or out of sight. It is a verb or noun. For example, 'She hid the gift before the party' means she put it somewhere others would not find it.

'Apply' means to make a formal request for something, or to put something onto a surface. Apply shows formal request or surface use. People notice submitting a request or spreading something. It is a verb. For example, 'Apply sunscreen before going outside' means spread it onto the skin.

'Competitive' means eager to win or having strong rivalry. Competitive shows desire to win. People notice rivalry or challenging environment. It is an adjective. For example, 'The job market is very competitive' means many people are competing for a limited number of positions.

'Crowd' refers to a large number of people gathered together. Crowd shows large group. People notice many people in one place. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'A large crowd gathered to watch the event' means many people came together to see it.

'Finding' refers to the result of research or investigation, or the act of discovering something. Finding shows discovered result. People notice a conclusion reached through study. 'Expressed' means communicated thoughts or feelings in words or actions. Expressed shows communicating feelings or ideas. People notice something shared openly. It is a verb. For example, 'She expressed her gratitude with a letter' means she communicated her thankfulness in writing.

'Sake' means for the purpose or benefit of something or someone. Sake shows reason or purpose. People notice doing something for a reason. It is a noun. For example, 'For the sake of safety, wear a helmet' means because safety is the reason.

'Underlying' means existing beneath or forming the basis of something. Underlying shows hidden basis. People notice something deeper or not immediately visible. It is an adjective. For example, 'the underlying cause of the problem' means the basic root cause that is not immediately obvious.

'Passing' means going by, or achieving the minimum standard required. Passing shows moving by or meeting a standard. People notice something going past or a minimum level reached. 'Weak' means lacking physical strength or being easily broken. Weak shows low strength or fragility. People notice little force or vulnerability. It is an adjective. 'Wet' means covered with or containing water. Wet shows liquid-covered state. People notice moisture on a surface. It is an adjective or verb. For example, 'My clothes are wet from the rain' means they are soaked with water.

'Lifted' means raised something upward, or improved a mood. Lifted shows upward movement or improvement. People notice something raised or a better feeling. It is a verb. 'Gentleman' refers to a man who behaves politely and with respect. Gentleman shows polite refined man. People notice respectful male behavior. It is a noun. For example, 'He held the door open like a true gentleman' means he acted in a polite and respectful way.

'Squeak' means to make a short high-pitched sound. Squeak shows high thin sound. People notice a small sharp noise. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'The mouse let out a squeak' means the small animal made a short high noise, and 'the door squeaks' means it makes a high sound when opened.

'Editor' refers to a person who checks and improves written work before publication, or software used to edit content. Editor shows correction role or editing tool. 'Desktop' refers to the main screen area of a computer, or a computer designed for use on a desk. Desktop shows computer workspace or desk computer type. 'Authorities' refers to people or organizations with official power over others, such as the police or government. Authorities shows official power figures. People notice those in charge. 'Planning' means thinking about and organizing what will be done in the future. Planning shows organizing future actions. People notice preparation or arrangement. It is a noun or verb. 'Relations' refers to the way in which people or groups behave toward each other. Relations shows connections or interactions. People notice how groups interact. It is a noun. For example, 'international relations' means the way different countries interact with each other.

'Counter' refers to a flat surface where things are placed or work is done, or to say something in opposition. Counter shows flat surface or opposition. 'Hungry' means feeling a need or desire for food. Hungry shows need for food. People notice an empty stomach sensation. It is an adjective. For example, 'I am very hungry after the long walk' means I need food after the physical activity.

'Unlikely' means not expected to happen or probably not true. Unlikely shows low probability. People notice something with little chance. It is an adjective. For example, 'It is unlikely to snow in summer' means there is very little chance of it happening.

'Narrow' means having a small distance from side to side. Narrow shows limited width. People notice small width or restricted space. It is an adjective or verb. For example, 'The road is too narrow for two cars' means there is not enough width for both.

'Nightly' means happening every night. Nightly shows nightly repetition. People notice something occurring each night. It is an adjective or adverb. For example, 'The news is broadcast nightly at ten' means it airs every single night at that time.

'Quarterly' means happening four times a year, once every three months. Quarterly shows every three months. People notice regular four-times-a-year pattern. It is an adjective or adverb. For example, 'The company releases quarterly reports' means financial reports four times a year.

'Employed' means having a paid job. Employed shows working state. People notice someone with a job. It is a verb or adjective. For example, 'She has been employed at the company for five years' means she has worked and been paid there for that time.

'Dragging' means pulling something heavy along a surface, or moving slowly. Dragging shows slow pulling movement. People notice something being pulled or a slow pace. It is a verb. For example, 'He was dragging the heavy bag across the floor' means pulling it with effort.

'Pole' is a long thin round stick or post, or one of the two extreme ends of the Earth. Pole shows long stick or Earth's extreme point. People notice a vertical post or geographic extreme. 'Mention' means to refer to something briefly or casually in conversation or writing. Mention shows brief reference. People notice something said without full detail. It is a verb or noun. For example, 'She mentioned she might be late' means she briefly said it without going into detail.

'Duty' refers to a task or action required as part of a job or moral responsibility. Duty shows obligation or responsibility. People notice required task. It is a noun. For example, 'It is your duty to report what you saw' means you are morally or officially required to do so.

'Crying' means producing tears and making sounds because of sadness or strong emotion. Crying shows emotional expression through tears. People notice someone upset or moved. It is a verb. For example, 'She was crying after hearing the sad news' means she shed tears and made sounds of grief.

'Partnership' means a relationship between two or more people or organizations working together. Partnership shows cooperative relationship. People notice shared work or business. It is a noun. 'Commodity' refers to a raw material or basic product that can be bought and sold. Commodity shows basic tradeable good. People notice a raw product with market value. It is a noun. 'Sin' refers to an act considered morally wrong, especially in a religious sense. Sin shows moral or religious wrongdoing. People notice a violation of moral rules. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'Lying is considered a sin in many religions' means it is seen as a morally wrong act.

'Governor' refers to the elected head of a state or region, or the person in charge of an institution. Governor shows regional leader or official head. 'Located' means situated or placed in a particular position. Located shows position or place. People notice where something is found. It is a verb or adjective. For example, 'The office is located on the third floor' means it is situated there.

'Combination' refers to a mix of two or more things joined together. Combination shows mixture or joining. People notice things put together. It is a noun. 'Raising' means lifting something up or increasing an amount, or bringing up children or animals. Raising shows lifting or increasing. People notice higher level or bringing up. It is a verb. 'Friendship' refers to a relationship between people who know, like, and trust each other. Friendship shows close mutual relationship. People notice bond between friends. It is a noun. 'Feelings' refers to emotional states or experiences, such as happiness or sadness. Feelings shows emotions experienced. People notice inner emotional state. It is a noun. For example, 'She kept her feelings to herself' means she did not share her emotional state with others.

'Concerning' means causing worry or anxiety, or relating to a topic. Concerning shows worrying quality or relevance. People notice something troubling or a subject being addressed. 'Recognized' means identified someone or something seen before, or acknowledged something as valid. Recognized shows identification or acknowledgment. 'Mostly' means for the most part or in the majority of cases. Mostly shows dominant amount. People notice that something is true most of the time. It is an adverb. For example, 'The work is mostly finished' means most of it is done but perhaps not all.

'Bringing' means carrying or taking something to a place. Bringing shows transporting or delivering. People notice something being carried somewhere. It is a verb. For example, 'She is bringing food to the party' means she is carrying it there.

'Maize' is a tall plant grown for its yellow grain, also known as corn. Maize shows grain crop. People notice a food plant with yellow seeds. It is a noun. For example, 'Maize is an important crop in many countries' means the plant is widely grown for food.

'Contents' refers to the things held inside something, or the list of what is in a book. Contents shows what is inside. People notice items within or a table of chapters. It is a noun. For example, 'The contents of the box were checked carefully' means everything inside it was examined.

'Reasonable' means fair and sensible, or not too expensive. Reasonable shows fair judgment or acceptable amount. People notice something sensible or affordable. It is an adjective. For example, 'a reasonable price' means one that seems fair and not too much.

'Organization' refers to a group of people working together for a shared goal, or the way something is arranged. Organization shows structured group or arrangement. 'Drawing' refers to a picture made with pencil or pen, or the act of creating one. Drawing shows pictorial creation. People notice a hand-made picture. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'He made a drawing of the building' means he created a picture of it using lines.

'Clop' is the sound a horse's hooves make when they strike a hard surface. Clop shows rhythmic hoof sound. People notice the tapping sound of a horse walking. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'We heard the clop of hooves on the cobblestones' means the regular striking sound of a horse walking.

'Arms' refers to the two upper limbs of the body, or weapons used in fighting. Arms shows body limbs or weapons. People notice upper body parts or military equipment. It is a noun. 'Ripe' means fully developed and ready to eat, or ready for a particular action. Ripe shows full development or readiness. People notice fruit ready to eat or a good moment. It is an adjective. For example, 'The bananas are ripe' means they have fully developed and are ready to eat.

'Waters' refers to areas or bodies of water, such as a sea, river, or lake. Waters shows areas of water. People notice large bodies of water. It is a noun. For example, 'The ship sailed through unknown waters' means across areas of sea that were not familiar.

'Vagina' is the medical term for the internal female reproductive organ and birth canal. Vagina shows female anatomy. People notice biological body structure. It is a noun. It is the correct anatomical term used in medical and educational contexts.

'Drinkable' means safe and suitable to drink. Drinkable shows safe consumption quality. People notice whether something is safe to consume as a liquid. It is an adjective. For example, 'Is the water drinkable?' means is it safe to drink without causing harm.

'Homepage' is the main page of a website that appears first when you visit it. Homepage shows main web entry page. People notice the starting point of a website. It is a noun. For example, 'Click the logo to return to the homepage' means the first and main page of the website.

'Handling' means dealing with or managing something. Handling shows managing or touching. People notice how something is managed or physically treated. It is a noun or verb. 'Sought' is the past tense of seek, meaning something was searched for or requested. Sought shows past searching or requesting. People notice something looked for in the past. It is a verb. For example, 'She sought help from her teacher' means she looked for and requested assistance.

'Energy' refers to the power to do work or be active, or a natural resource used for power. Energy shows capacity for activity or power source. People notice vitality or fuel for work. It is a noun. For example, 'She has a lot of energy in the morning' means she feels very active and lively then.
'Quickly' means at a fast speed. Quickly shows fast pace. People notice rapid action. It is an adverb. For example, 'She answered the question quickly' means she responded at a fast speed.

'Accord' refers to an official agreement between parties, or to give or grant something. Accord shows official agreement or granting. People notice a formal deal or something given. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'The two countries signed a peace accord' means a formal agreement between them.

'Extraordinary' means very unusual or remarkable. Extraordinary shows rare and impressive quality. People notice something beyond the ordinary. It is an adjective. For example, 'She has an extraordinary talent for music' means one that is remarkably rare and impressive.

'Disabled' means having a condition that limits physical or mental abilities, or having a feature turned off. Disabled shows limited ability or deactivated feature. People notice a person with limited abilities or a turned-off function. It is an adjective or verb. For example, 'The feature has been disabled in the settings' means turned off.

'Changing' means becoming different or making something different. Changing shows transformation in progress. People notice something in the process of becoming different. It is a verb or adjective. For example, 'The weather is always changing' means it is constantly becoming different.

'Committee' refers to a group of people chosen to manage or make decisions about a specific matter. Committee shows decision-making group. People notice a formal organized group. It is a noun. For example, 'The committee met to discuss the new proposal' means the group gathered to consider it.

'Stopped' means came to a halt or prevented something from continuing. Stopped shows halted state. People notice something that ended or was prevented. It is a verb. For example, 'She stopped running when she reached the finish line' means she came to a halt there.

'Spirit' refers to the non-physical part of a person, or a strong feeling of attitude. Spirit shows inner essence or strong feeling. People notice inner vitality or attitude. It is a noun. For example, 'Team spirit helped them win' means the shared positive attitude of the group, and 'a free spirit' means someone who lives freely and independently.

'Deck' refers to a flat surface on a ship, or a set of playing cards, or an outdoor floor area. Deck shows ship floor, cards, or outdoor area. People notice a ship's floor, a card set, or a wooden outdoor area. It is a noun. For example, 'They stood on the deck watching the sea' means the flat outer floor of the ship.

'Revised' means changed or updated to improve or correct. Revised shows updated or corrected version. People notice something improved through changes. It is a verb or adjective. For example, 'She submitted a revised draft' means an updated and corrected version.

'Planned' means decided in advance or arranged. Planned shows pre-arranged action. People notice something organized ahead of time. It is a verb or adjective. For example, 'The trip was carefully planned' means it was organized well in advance.

'Strength' refers to the quality of being physically strong, or the capacity to withstand pressure. Strength shows power or endurance. People notice physical or mental power. It is a noun. For example, 'She showed great strength throughout the difficult time' means powerful ability to endure.

'Shot' means firing a weapon, taking a photograph, or an attempt at something. Shot shows fired projectile, photo, or attempt. People notice a fired bullet, a taken picture, or a try. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'She took a shot at goal' means she attempted to score, and 'take a shot with the camera' means take a photograph.

'Payment' refers to the act of paying money or the amount paid. Payment shows money given. People notice money transferred for goods or services. It is a noun. For example, 'The payment was made on time' means the money was given when required.

'Bus' is a large vehicle for carrying many passengers on a fixed route. Bus shows large public transport vehicle. People notice a vehicle carrying many people. It is a noun. For example, 'She takes the bus to school every morning' means the large public vehicle.

'Clean' means free from dirt or impurities, or to make something free from dirt. Clean shows absence of dirt or the act of removing it. People notice something without dirt or the activity of cleaning. It is an adjective or verb. For example, 'The kitchen was very clean' means free of dirt, and 'clean the floor' means remove the dirt from it.

'Direction' refers to the path or course along which something moves, or guidance on what to do. Direction shows course of movement or guidance. People notice which way something goes or instructions given. It is a noun. For example, 'Walk in the direction of the station' means toward it, and 'follow the directions' means the instructions given.

'Seeing' means using the eyes to observe, or noticing something. Seeing shows visual observation. People notice someone using their eyes. It is a verb. For example, 'I am seeing improvements in her work' means I am noticing them.

'Taste' refers to the sensation of flavor in the mouth, or the ability to judge quality. Taste shows flavor sensation or judgment. People notice a flavor or a sense of quality. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'The food has a wonderful taste' means flavor, and 'she has good taste in clothes' means good judgment in style.

'Extra' means beyond what is usual or necessary. Extra shows additional amount. People notice something more than normal. It is an adjective, adverb, or noun. For example, 'She did extra work to finish on time' means work beyond what was required.

'Launch' means to start something new officially, or to send something into motion. Launch shows starting or sending off. People notice something new beginning. It is a verb or noun. For example, 'The company will launch its new product next week' means officially introduce it to the public.

'Cast' refers to all the actors in a film or play, or to throw something with force. Cast shows group of performers or throwing action. People notice actors or throwing. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'The cast of the film was excellent' means all the actors in it, and 'cast the fishing line' means throw it into the water.

'Details' refers to individual pieces of specific information. Details shows specific information. People notice particular small facts. It is a noun. For example, 'Please send me the details of the meeting' means the specific information about it.

'Response' refers to a reply or reaction to something. Response shows reply or reaction. People notice an answer given. It is a noun. For example, 'She received a quick response to her email' means a fast reply.

'Seeking' means trying to find or obtain something. Seeking shows active searching. People notice looking for something. It is a verb. For example, 'She is seeking a new job' means she is actively trying to find one.

'Title' refers to the name of a book, film, or work, or a word showing someone's rank. Title shows name of a work or rank designation. People notice a name given to something or a formal address. It is a noun. For example, 'What is the title of the book?' means its name, and 'her title is Doctor' means her formal rank.

'Mode' refers to a way or method of doing something, or a setting on a device. Mode shows method or device setting. People notice a particular way of operating. It is a noun. For example, 'Switch to silent mode' means change the device setting to make no sound.

'Boom' refers to a period of rapid economic growth, or a loud deep sound. Boom shows rapid growth or deep sound. People notice sudden rapid increase or a deep explosive sound. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'The economy is experiencing a boom' means rapid growth, and 'the sound of a boom' means a loud deep noise.

'Hang' means to attach something from above so it swings freely, or to spend time. Hang shows attaching from above or spending time. People notice something suspended or time spent casually. It is a verb. For example, 'Hang the painting on the wall' means attach it from above, and 'hang out with friends' means spend time casually.
'Happen' means to occur or take place. Happen shows occurring event. People notice something taking place. It is a verb. For example, 'What will happen next?' means what event will occur.

'Installing' means setting up and putting something in place for use. Installing shows setting up process. People notice something being made ready for use. It is a verb. For example, 'She is installing new software on the computer' means setting it up so it can be used.

'Pants' refers to clothing worn on the lower body covering each leg separately. Pants shows lower body clothing. People notice trousers or leggings. It is a noun. For example, 'He wore black pants to the meeting' means the lower body garment covering both legs.

'Takeover' refers to an act of gaining control of something, especially a company. Takeover shows gaining control. People notice one entity taking control of another. It is a noun. For example, 'The company was the target of a hostile takeover' means another company tried to gain control of it by force.

'Warning' refers to a statement alerting someone to danger or a problem. Warning shows alerting statement. People notice a signal of danger. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'She gave a warning before starting the difficult exercise' means she told people to be careful before beginning.

'Difference' refers to a way in which things are unlike each other, or the result of subtracting one number from another. Difference shows unlike quality or subtraction result. People notice how things are not the same. It is a noun. For example, 'What is the difference between the two?' means in what way are they unlike.

'Analyst' refers to a person who examines information to draw conclusions. Analyst shows examining professional. People notice someone interpreting data or situations. It is a noun. For example, 'The analyst predicted a rise in prices' means the person who examined the data and drew a conclusion.

'Failure' refers to not achieving what was intended, or something that stops working. Failure shows not succeeding. People notice a lack of success or breakdown. It is a noun. For example, 'The project ended in failure' means it did not achieve its intended goal.

'Pact' refers to a formal agreement between two or more parties. Pact shows formal agreement. People notice a mutual deal or treaty. It is a noun. For example, 'The two countries signed a pact to avoid conflict' means a formal mutual agreement.

'Considered' means thought about carefully, or regarded as something. Considered shows careful thought or being regarded. People notice careful deliberation or an assigned label. It is a verb or adjective. For example, 'She is considered the best in her field' means regarded as such by others.

'Trouble' refers to difficulty, problems, or a situation causing worry. Trouble shows problems or difficulty. People notice something causing difficulty. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'She had trouble sleeping' means difficulty doing so, and 'do not trouble yourself' means do not worry.

'Ability' refers to the power or skill to do something. Ability shows skill or capacity. People notice someone's capability. It is a noun. For example, 'She has the ability to learn very quickly' means the skill and capacity to do so.

'Mad' means very angry, or mentally ill, or informally very enthusiastic. Mad shows strong anger or mental disorder or enthusiasm. People notice intense emotion or unusual mental state. It is an adjective. For example, 'She was mad at him for forgetting' means very angry, and 'mad about football' means very enthusiastic.

'Born' means having come into existence through birth. Born shows beginning of life. People notice the start of someone's life. It is a verb or adjective. For example, 'She was born in Seoul' means her life began there.

'Pregnant' means carrying a developing baby inside the body. Pregnant shows expecting a baby. People notice a woman expecting a child. It is an adjective. For example, 'She is pregnant and expecting her baby in spring' means she is carrying a developing child.

'Bug' refers to a small insect, or an error in a computer program, or to annoy someone. Bug shows small insect, software error, or annoyance. People notice an insect, a program error, or feeling bothered. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'There is a bug in the code' means an error, and 'bugs in the garden' means small insects.

'Certainly' means without any doubt, or used to express strong agreement. Certainly shows absolute certainty or confident agreement. People notice a strong and clear affirmation. It is an adverb. For example, 'I will certainly be there' means there is no doubt I will attend.

'Balanced' means having equal or proportionate amounts, or stable and steady. Balanced shows equal proportion or stability. People notice something fair or steady. It is an adjective or verb. For example, 'a balanced diet' means one with the right amounts of all food types.
'Begin' means to start doing something. Begin shows starting action. People notice the start of something. It is a verb. For example, 'We will begin the meeting at nine' means start it at that time.

'Girlfriend' refers to a woman with whom someone is in a romantic relationship. Girlfriend shows romantic female partner. People notice a close romantic relationship. It is a noun. For example, 'He introduced his girlfriend to his parents' means the woman he is romantically involved with.

'Stage' refers to a raised platform for performances, or a particular point in a process. Stage shows performance platform or process point. People notice a place for performing or a step in progress. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'The band walked onto the stage' means the raised platform, and 'at this stage of the project' means this particular point in the process.

'Feeling' refers to an emotional state or a physical sensation. Feeling shows emotion or physical sensation. People notice something experienced inside. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'She had a feeling of joy' means an emotional state of happiness.

'Usually' means under normal circumstances or most of the time. Usually shows typical pattern. People notice what happens most of the time. It is an adverb. For example, 'She usually arrives at eight' means that is what normally happens.

'Sincerely' means in a genuine and honest way, without pretending. Sincerely shows genuine feeling or expression. People notice a true and heartfelt manner. It is an adverb. For example, 'I sincerely hope you feel better soon' means I truly and genuinely hope so. It is also commonly used at the end of formal letters before signing your name.

'Enclose' means to include something inside a letter or package, or to surround something with a barrier. Enclose shows including inside or surrounding. People notice something included with a document or a surrounded area. It is a verb. For example, 'Please find the document enclosed with this letter' means included inside the envelope along with the letter.

'Notify' means to officially inform someone about something. Notify shows official informing. People notice being told something important in a formal way. It is a verb. For example, 'Please notify us if your address changes' means officially inform us of the change so we have the correct information.

'Upcoming' means about to happen or arrive soon. Upcoming shows near future event. People notice something that has not happened yet but will soon. It is an adjective. For example, 'She is preparing for the upcoming exam' means the one that will take place soon.

'Accordingly' means in a way that is appropriate to the situation, or as a result. Accordingly shows appropriate action or logical consequence. People notice a response that fits the situation. It is an adverb. For example, 'The rules have changed, so please act accordingly' means change your behavior to match the new rules.

'Supervisor' refers to a person who watches over and directs the work of others. Supervisor shows person in charge of others. People notice someone managing a team or workers. It is a noun. For example, 'She reported the problem to her supervisor' means the person responsible for overseeing her work.

'Applicant' refers to a person who formally applies for something such as a job or a place at university. Applicant shows person making a formal request. People notice someone seeking something through an official process. It is a noun. For example, 'All applicants must submit their documents by Friday' means everyone formally applying must do so by then.

'Eligible' means meeting the necessary requirements to qualify for something. Eligible shows meeting the conditions required. People notice whether someone is allowed or qualified. It is an adjective. For example, 'You are eligible to apply if you have two years of experience' means you meet the requirements to do so.

'Invoice' refers to an official document listing goods or services provided and the amount owed. Invoice shows official payment request document. People notice a bill showing what must be paid. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'The company sent an invoice for the work completed' means a document requesting payment for the service.

'Warranty' refers to a written guarantee that a product will be repaired or replaced if it has problems within a set time. Warranty shows official product guarantee. People notice a promise of repair or replacement. It is a noun. For example, 'The washing machine comes with a two-year warranty' means if it breaks within two years, it will be fixed or replaced at no extra cost.

'Refund' refers to a sum of money returned to a customer when goods or services are unsatisfactory. Refund shows returned money. People notice money given back after a complaint or return. It is a noun or verb. For example, 'She requested a refund because the product was damaged' means she asked for her money back.

'Receipt' refers to a written document confirming that money has been paid or goods have been received. Receipt shows proof of payment or delivery. People notice a document confirming a transaction. It is a noun. For example, 'Keep your receipt in case you need to return the item' means the document proving you paid for it.

'Itinerary' refers to a detailed plan or schedule of a journey, listing places to visit and times. Itinerary shows travel plan schedule. People notice an organized list of travel activities. It is a noun. For example, 'The travel agent provided a full itinerary for the trip' means a document listing every stop and activity during the journey.

'Reservation' refers to an arrangement to have something kept for your use at a future time, such as a table at a restaurant or a hotel room. Reservation shows advance booking. People notice something set aside for them in advance. It is a noun. For example, 'She made a reservation at the restaurant for seven o'clock' means she arranged in advance to have a table available at that time.

'Luggage' refers to bags and suitcases that a traveler carries. Luggage shows travel bags and cases. People notice the bags someone brings on a trip. It is a noun. For example, 'She checked her luggage at the airport before boarding' means her bags were registered and stored in the aircraft.

'Brochure' refers to a small booklet or folded sheet containing information about a product, service, or place. Brochure shows promotional informational booklet. People notice a printed document used to share information or advertise. It is a noun. For example, 'She picked up a brochure about the hotel at the tourist office' means a small printed booklet describing the hotel.

'Merchandise' refers to goods that are bought and sold. Merchandise shows tradeable goods. People notice products available for purchase. It is a noun. For example, 'The store had a wide range of merchandise on display' means many different types of goods available to buy.

'Subscription' refers to an arrangement where you pay regularly to receive a service or publication. Subscription shows regular payment for continued access. People notice a regular payment for ongoing access. It is a noun. For example, 'She has a monthly subscription to a streaming service' means she pays each month to continue using it.

'Renovation' refers to the process of repairing and improving a building or room. Renovation shows repair and improvement work. People notice construction activity to make a place better. It is a noun. For example, 'The kitchen is closed for renovation' means it is being repaired and improved and is temporarily unavailable.
